title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus generated countless Humanity Phantoms and seeped among the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and mutating their bodies, their bloated heads lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and brain parts protruding from cracks. Corrupted Oolacile sorcerers discovered abyssal sorceries, more weighty and dealing physical damage instead of magical, since the Dark produced sorceries with a more tangible, "human" presence.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Kaathe, following his failure with the Four Kings, arrived in Oolacile and manipulated its inhabitants into upturning the grave of Manus, a primordial man with an extraordinary Dark Soul and dark sorcery skills, who had been buried beneath the dungeons of their city, and resurrect him. Awakening to find his precious broken pendant missing, Manus was eventually driven mad and his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into a dark beast eternally seeking his pendant. His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus not only generated countless Humanity Phantoms with a will of their own but also influenced the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and horribly mutating their bodies, bloating their head and opening them with cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and protruding brain parts.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus was a sorcerer of Oolacile, and after he died, his body was buried in the caverns beneath the city. 200 to 300 years prior to the journey of the Chosen Undead, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe arrived in Oolacile, in search of a potential Dark Lord following the flooding of New Londo. He manipulated the country to upturn the grave of the primordial man, Manus, buried beneath the dungeons of their city and resurrect him. Manus awakened to find his pendant missing, and was eventually driven into a beastly frenzy as his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into the "Father of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Despite this, when returning to the current age and speaking to Dusk, she would simply note that the Chosen Undead looks a lot like Artorias (believing it was Artorias who rescued her from Manus), without expanding on whether or not the Chosen Undead's actions had any effect in saving Oolacile.

While speaking to Marvelous Chester, he would say that "Oolacile has brought the Abyss upon itself [...] Fooled by that toothy serpent, they upturned the grave of primeval man, and incited his ornery wrath", implying that either Kingseeker Frampt or Darkstalker Kaathe had a hand in Oolacile's downfall. Due to the inherent darkness of the Abyss, Darkstalker Kaathe is the more likely culprit.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - plot 
 plot : Once the Chosen Undead has the Broken Pendant in their possession, Manus pulls them through a magical rift from Darkroot Basin into the past land of Oolacile.

He kidnapped Princess Dusk and is eventually confronted in the Chasm of the Abyss.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As the Abyss continued to spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience from fighting the Abyss and its creatures in New Londo. However, Artorias's silver pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Artorias, together with his trusted companion Sif, nevertheless faced Manus, but his strength proved insufficient to defeat the Father of the Abyss. Wounded in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier to protect Sif against the Dark. Artorias, his soul corrupted by the Abyss and his armor corroded, was left alone in his fight against the Abyssal creatures of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. His prized pendant eventually came under the possession of a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead encountered Knight Artorias, who had retained only the very last vestige of his sanity in the battle against the Abyss, still desperate to put down the corrupted creatures of Oolacile. During the fight that ensued between him and the Chosen Undead, Artorias succumbed to the Abyss entirely, and was finally defeated by the Undead.

Ciaran, who had arrived at the arena where Artorias was corrupted by the Abyss, also requested the Soul of Artorias from the Chosen Undead who had finally put an end to the knight's suffering, with the intention of paying proper respects to her passed dear friend.

title: Oolacile Township Dungeon
snippet:
Oolacile Township Dungeon -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : In addition to the Oolacile Township and Chasm of the Abyss, Manus, Father of the Abyss acts as the area boss for the Oolacile Township Dungeon for summoning and invasion purposes.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: The Abyss Watchers established dominion over Farron Keep, the swampland once known as Oolacile or Darkroot Garden. Here they closely guarded what was once the Chasm of the Abyss, the cradle of Manus and a seedbed for Abyssal beasts; these headquarters would also have been in close proximity to Artorias's tomb. The Watchers gained notoriety due to their scorched-earth approach to containing outbreaks of the Abyss, destroying kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Nonetheless, many would enlist as their followers in a bid to partake of wolf's blood and become part of the Undead Legion.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The lost land of **Oolacile** is a location that no longer exists by the events of *Dark Souls*. Several sources allude to its existence centuries beforehand and its focus on sorceries. Dusk of Oolacile states that the land "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The later version of the game, *Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition*, comes with extra content that takes place in Oolacile 200-300 years before the events of the game, where the Chosen Undead must take the place of Artorias the Abysswalker and rescue Dusk from Manus, Father of the Abyss. During this period, Oolacile is slowly being swallowed by the Abyss. The content was later added as DLC to the console versions of the game as *Artorias of the Abyss*.

title: Oolacile Township
snippet:
Oolacile Township -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : Although Knight Artorias is fought here, Manus, Father of the Abyss acts as the area boss for the Oolacile Township, Oolacile Township Dungeon, and the Chasm of the Abyss for summoning and invasion purposes.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - artorias_of_the_abyss 
 artorias_of_the_abyss : In *Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition* or *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC, the Chosen Undead passes through part of Oolacile after traveling into the past; however, despite it taking place centuries before the rest of the game, the Oolacile Township is still fraught with hopelessness. The township has become filled with enemies (specifically Bloatheads, Bloathead Sorcerers, and a Chained Prisoner) as the Abyss spreads, and is seemingly deserted.

One of the Four Knights of Gwyn, Artorias the Abysswalker, arrived in Oolacile to rescue Dusk of Oolacile from Manus, Father of the Abyss, but fell victim to the Abyss. By the time the Chosen Undead found him, Artorias was hostile and engaged them in combat. After the Chosen Undead defeated the brave knight, they finish what Artorias had started, continuing through Oolacile Township and onward, eventually defeating Manus and rescuing Dusk.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - artorias_of_the_abyss 
 artorias_of_the_abyss : Dusk's summon sign vanishes from Darkroot Basin after the Chosen Undead obtains the Broken Pendant. After being pulled into a nearby dark void and transported to the past land of Oolacile, the Chosen Undead discovers that Dusk has been abducted by Manus, Father of the Abyss.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : Manus is the final boss of the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC. He is encountered in the Chasm of the Abyss.

It is possible to summon the past version of Great Gray Wolf Sif to aid in the battle. Sif's summon sign is found in the arena where the player fights Manus, inside the fog door.

title: Soul of Manus
snippet:
Soul of Manus -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Manus, Father of the Abyss. This extraordinary soul is a viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity.

Ancient Manus was clearly once human. But he became the Father of the Abyss after his humanity went wild, eternally seeking his precious broken pendant.

title: Chasm of the Abyss
snippet:
Chasm of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : Located at the lower portion of Oolacile, it is found after the player exits the Oolacile Township Dungeon, and a shortcut to the Royal Wood can be opened via an elevator. In this area, the player will fight Manus, Father of the Abyss, the final boss of the DLC. At the bottom of the chasm, a circle of stones surrounding a grave can be found, alluding to the upturned grave of Primeval Man.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:

 attacks : {'name': 'Abyss Cage', 'description': 'Dark Orbs propagate from above Manus, surrounding the entire arena before homing back in on Manus. This attack covers the entire arena, except for the area right next to Manus, like an inverted AoE. Dodge it by getting as close as possible to Manus once he starts casting. The Silver Pendant can also block this attack.'}

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: Finally, the Chosen Undead arrives at the Chasm of the Abyss where an illusion of Alvina guides the player to an illusory wall. Inside, the Chosen Undead discovers an injured Sif, protected by a magic barrier created by Artorias, in order to prevent Sif from being engulfed. Shortly after rescuing Sif the player faces Manus, Father of the Abyss, who is responsible for the spread of the dark. Manus is defeated, and Princess Dusk is saved. Upon returning to Oolacile Sanctuary, they are greeted by Elizabeth, who tells the Chosen Undead that she will let everyone know that Artorias was the one who defeated Manus, so that his honor may prevail. However, she assures them that their great deed will not be forgotten.

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: Sometime around the fall of Oolacile, Gough arrived at the kingdom in response to the uncontrollable expansion of Manus' Abyss. However, he was imprisoned by the citizens of the country in a tower sealed by powerful magic. The eye holes of his helm were packed with tree resin by those who dismissed the force of the giant as brutish, indicating racist sentiments of many towards the giants.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: The Chosen Undead further journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the honor and the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - plot 
 plot : Traveling to the land of Oolacile can only be done after obtaining the Broken Pendant, which is dropped by a Crystal Golem in The Duke's Archives after speaking with Dusk of Oolacile. Approaching the area where Dusk is initially saved, with the Pendant in one's possession, will reveal a shadowy portal, which the player examines.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As centuries passed, the ruins of Oolacile overgrew into the "Darkroot Garden", where the remnants of the ancient Guardians of the city still patrol the area as Stone Knights. Sif survived the battle with Manus thanks to the intervention of the Chosen Undead. The wolf inherited Artorias's divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias's tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias's rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead who arrived with the intention of plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the First Flame continued to wane, an Abyss opened beneath Drangleic, the result of the scattered fragments of an ancient abyss and the dissipated Manus, Father of the Abyss. Coalescing again, this abyss expanded across the region and assimilated all things into its growth, with its darkness felt even by those attuned to magic in neighbouring regions. A group of Undead led by Darkdiver Grandahl, called the Pilgrims of Dark, started to make pilgrimages to what they considered holy sites and delved into the Dark Chasm, to overcome the trials that lurked in the depths to refine the darkness within them. In the heart of the abyss, the Darklurker manifested: A dark, angelic creature that manipulated darkness along with sorcery, pyromancy and miracles and demonstrated superhuman abilities.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Kaathe resides in the darkness of the Abyss, but seems to be more involved in the affairs of Lordran than Frampt. Kaathe gave the Four Kings the art of lifedrain and consequently founded the Darkwraith covenant. He also seems to have tricked the residents of Oolacile into uncovering the corpse of Manus, driving him mad in the process. This sparked the spread of the Abyss, transforming the townsfolk into monstrous beings whose humanity has run wild, akin to Manus.

In the ending of Dark Lord, ten additional primordial serpents are seen, whose names are unknown. They appear to want to serve the newly-appointed Dark Lord, and possibly usher in the Age of Dark. An interesting note in this ending is that Kaathe states that both himself and Frampt will serve the Chosen Undead, disregarding any actions the player has taken before reaching this point, like placing the Lordvessel with Frampt instead of Kaathe, which would make the latter refuse to cooperate with the player, and vice-versa.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Manus was a primordial human who possessed an extraordinary soul consisting of a viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity, an immense Dark Soul. He was also a sorcerer who used a rough and old wooden catalyst, very crude but large enough to be used as a weapon. His sorceries could grant a fleeting will to the Dark of humanity, induced to relentlessly chase enemies through channeling innate human affinities. Manus also possessed one half of an ancient stone pendant, a precious magical artifact that emanated a distinct, wrenching nostalgia as well as reverence.

title: Bloated Head
snippet:
Bloated Head -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : The head of an Oolacile resident whose humanity went wild after being devoured by the Dark of Manus, father of the Abyss.

The bloated head is fissured, the cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs with a hard outside and mucous-filled inside, no sane person could ever wear it.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: Eventually, the Watchers linked the Fire, although it is unknown if one or all had done so. With the Watchers becoming Lords of Cinder, the wolf blood dried up. The Followers, now having nothing to live for, went hollow, roaming the land and eventually disappearing into the Painted World of Ariandel. With no one remaining to execute the corrupted, the acolytes were slowly devolved by the Abyss, and Farron was consumed in a rotting bog. When the Abyss Watchers were awakened to kindle the Flame once again, they returned home to find it corrupted and their mission unsuccessful. The Watchers in the keep now fight against themselves, endlessly slaying their brethren corrupted by the Abyss.

snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Dusk is from the ancient and long-dead land of Oolacile, which practiced magic alien even to the magic realm of Vinheim. It is unknown how she was trapped in the Golem in the first place, but it is clear that she is in the wrong era.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Dusk appears to believe that she was saved by Artorias, as told by the legend, while in actuality she was saved by the Chosen Undead. While unaware that Artorias had been corrupted by the Abyss before he could save her, Dusk's senses do hint that the Chosen Undead bears the same "resonance" as her fabled savior, leading her to question the details of her temporarily intangible captivity.
The feelings that she sensed during her imprisonment in the Abyss—"*a wrenching nostalgia, a lost joy, an object of obsession, and a sincere hope to reclaim it"—*are evocative of the "shards" of Manus present in Drangleic, who each represented a form of longing; namely Nadalia, Alsanna, Nashandra and Elana.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Manus may be named for Mannus, the father of mankind in Germanic mythology. According to the Roman writer Tacitus, the Germanic tribes believed a god *Tuisto* sprang from the ground and had a son, *Mannus*, from whom all humans were descended. Manus is also the Latin word for “hand”, alluding to Manus’s massive left hand.
**However a more accurate translation of "深淵の主マヌス" would be "Manus, Lord of the Abyss".

title: Humans
snippet: Meanwhile, in a place called Oolacile, the land of golden sorceries, humans loyal to the Gods were convinced by the Darkwraith leader named Kaathe, a primordial serpent loyal to the Pygmy, to raise up a primeval man who had been buried there. He went mad, and his Humanity bubbled over from his uncontrollable rage, mutating him into a dark monster. His Humanity overflowed and consumed the very world around him, generating another Abyss, and corrupting the citizens of Oolacile. Knight Artorias, one of the four knights of Gwyn, would be tasked to face the outbreak of the Abyss, only to be corrupted by it.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: After being dragged back in time, the Chosen Undead wakes up inside a cave beneath some trees. Outside, they are confronted by the Sanctuary Guardian. After slaying the beast, the Chosen Undead finds some sort of garden temple where they encounter a giant, talking mushroom named Elizabeth, who informs the player that the realm of Oolacile is being consumed by the darkness of the Abyss, She also tells the player that Princess Dusk has been kidnapped by a creature from the abyss and that Knight Artorias has ventured unto Oolacile to put an end to the spread. However, she assures the player that Artorias will be overwhelmed by the darkness.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: During their quest in Oolacile the Chosen Undead also meets Marvelous Chester, a somewhat sinister merchant who, like the player, was dragged into the past. He reveals to the Chosen Undead that the spread of the dark was caused when the inhabitants of Oolacile opened the grave of the primeval man due to the influence of a "toothy serpent". The Chosen Undead then treads through Oolacile Township in search of the dark source.

title: Lords
snippet: Darkstalker Kaathe, who opposed Gwyn's actions, attempted to bring about the Age of Dark and the coming of its ruler, the Dark Lord; most travelling to Oolacile and manipulating the citizens into upturning the grave of "primordial man". This resulted in Oolacile's fall as it began to be swallowed by the Abyss, consuming the land and corrupting its citizens. Kaathe also went to New Londo, seducing the Four Kings with the art of lifedrain, which corrupted them and their knights. In an effort to contain his darkwraiths, New Londo was flooded -an act that ultimately cost the lives of the city's inhabitants.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: However, the rest of the firstborn's reign was marked by catastrophes. The Four Kings of New Londo were corrupted by the dark power of Darkstalker Kaathe, starting to sow devastation nearby the city of the gods. Following Knight Artorias's failure to defeat the Darkwraiths, the gods were forced to flood the city, sacrificing all the humans within, and seal it. A similar event happened in Oolacile when, again due to Kaathe, the awakening of the primordial human Manus and his fury led to the collapse of the country when Artorias was unable to defeat him. In addition to the grave situation on the borders of Anor Londo, the city of the gods itself became a dangerous place when a group of cultists began targeting the clan of Gwyn and their kind, and occult weapons capable of killing the gods reached inside the walls of Anor Londo. Furthermore, in the city of the gods Seath the Scaleless had now completely lost his mind, transforming his Archives into a prison and going so far as to kidnap

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet: This is an indication to locate the three Knights of Eleum Loyce so that they may provide aid against the Ivory King. Once the Ivory King has been defeated, Alsanna will thank the player and reveal some more of her background and her connection to Manus, Father of the Abyss:

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: At some point Alsanna reached Eleum Loyce and became close to the Ivory King. She was in truth a fragment of the Dark Soul of Manus, Father of the Abyss, that, despite the fact that he had been killed centuries in the past, had retained some of his will and power. Alsanna was born as the incarnation of Manus' fears and despite being a frightened and frail thing she managed to to coalesce once again absorbing the other humanities, and then obtain the shape of a human, with her own self-awareness. To sustain herself and seek more power, she sought the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strenght. Alsanna thus sought the Ivory King to sustain herself and smother her innate fear and was accepted by him, quietly finding a place at the side of the leader of Eleum Loyce where he provided her comfort and she accepted Eleum Loyce as her home.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet: However, at a certain point, a Chosen Undead who ended up in Oolacile challenged the black dragon and after a legendary battle managed to defeat him. From his tail they formed an Obsidian Greatsword infused with the mystical power of the dragon and with his orange eye they created an enchanted ring that doubled the damaged received by its wearer.

title: Elizabeth
snippet: After the successful rescue of Oolacile's crown princess, she thanks the hero, but decides against sharing the truth of the tale, leading the heroic deed to be associated with Artorias instead. She also refuses to elucidate Dusk on the true nature of the beast that had kidnapped her, despite her many requests.

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: He witnessed the fall of Oolacile caused by their arrogance and greed, as well as Artorias' failure to quell the Abyss and his demise at the hands of the Chosen Undead. Should the time traveling hero choose to engage the legendary Kalameet, a dragon so fierce not even Anor Londo dared to cross him, Gough could even be allowed one last hunt, firing an impressive shot in spite of his now limited vision, speaking to the true might of the legendary archer. Having done that, though, he'll give away his precious bow, officially leaving that life behind him.

title: Lords
snippet:
One of Gwyn's four knights, Artorias, and his wolf companion Sif made a covenant with the beings of the Abyss that allowed him to traverse it, so that he could hunt the Darkwraiths. Artorias later arrived in Oolacile in an attempt to combat the spread of the Abyss, but was overcome and was forced to sacrifice his greatshield to save Sif. This left him unprotected from the Abyss, and he later became corrupted and driven to madness.

The Way of White was usurped by Gwyn's uncle, Lloyd, who also would start hunts against the Undead.

Eventually, the undead were corralled into several asylums to await the end of the world, for it is prophesied by Astora - who themselves inherited the prophecy from Frampt - that one day an undead will escape the prison and succeed Gwyn in linking the fire. At the same time, Kaathe preaches that this chosen has the opportunity to become the new Dark Lord and usher in the Age of Dark.

title: Bastille Lord
snippet:
His fear became so vast and overwhelming that he quickly turned to worse methods to rid himself of the horrible blight. When the Bastille had become too full of afflicted humans, he ordered his monstrous Flexile Sentries to round up as many of them as possible into flimsy ships, to hurl them into the ocean and have them die at sea, away from land. Among them were the sorcerers of his country, some of which would survive the horrible punishment and find their way to a southern land where they established their own kingdom.

Despite all the measures he took to prevent his kingdom from falling victim to the fading of its era, the Bastille Lord could not stop the march of time. Olaphis would crumble into obscurity, and with the passage of time, the land would come to be known first as Venn, then as Drangleic. The ruins of his castle still stand, rotting away with some of its original, undying captives.

title: Mushroom People
snippet:
Mushroom People -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The time of Lothric wasn't kind to the forest-dwelling Mushroom People. For a time they lived in the forest of Farron, undisturbed, and were even regarded as divine beings by the Xanthous Scholars, researchers who wished to learn more about the lost country of Oolacile.

However, they would meet a rather violent end at the hands of the Ghrus, who emerged after the forest was consumed by a poisonous bog, a process that began when the Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame. What can be presumed to be the calcified remains of Elizabeth can also be found in a hidden cave containing the clothes of Princess Dusk and a scroll full of sorceries of Oolacile. It's unclear if some of the Mushroom People still exist far away from the rotted forest, or if they faced extinction after the Ghru's arrival.

title: Lothric
snippet: The fading of the Flame and the erosion of their faith made the citizens of Lothric more and more desperate, some of whom were transformed into humanoid trees that were turned in prayer towards Lothric Castle. Furthermore, the undead of the city began to show signs of an epidemic, in which their Dark Soul would explode from their bodies and manifest as an amorphous black blob with bestial features which attacked anything with destructive ferocity. The infestation of these Pus of Man led to the permanent closure of the Grand Archives' doors, with the scholars isolating themselves from the desperate situation of the kingdom to continue their work.

title: Sorcery (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Sorcery (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - lore 
 lore : Sorcery is said to have originated with Seath the Scaleless, the "grandfather of sorcery". The ancient land of Oolacile has its own sorceries, which are an "approximation" when compared to modern Sorcery and are characterized by augmenting the weapon or body, rather than causing offensive damage. Manus, Father of the Abyss is the source of at least one Abyss sorcery.

The other Abyss sorceries are said to be discovered by an Oolacile sorcerer on the brink of madness, they differ from normal offensive sorceries, which are derived from souls, in that they draw power from humanity and cause both Magic and Physical Damage due to their "weighty" nature.

Big Hat Logan of the Dragon School in Vinheim played a role in the development of numerous sorceries. During his infatuation with Seath in the Regal Archives, Logan developed new sorceries and boosted existing ones.

title: Bloated Sorcerer Head
snippet:
Bloated Sorcerer Head -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : The head of an Oolacile resident whose humanity went wild after being devoured by the Dark of manus, father of the Abyss.

The bloated head is fissured, the cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and accented by protuding brain parts. It is lightly enchanted, suggesting that it may have belonged to a sorcerer.

The will feels envy, or perhaps love, and despite the inevitably trite and tragic ending, the will sees no alternative, and is driven madly toward its target.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Alvina is a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire and is capable of human speech. At one point she became a trusted friend of Knight Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, as well as his companion Great Grey Wolf Sif.

After Artorias' death, Alvina moved to the ruins of Oolacile, now overgrown and known as the "Darkroot Garden", where the knight had succumbed in his fight against the Abyss of Manus. Sif too had moved here after he survived the battle with Manus and inherited Artorias' divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross into the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias' tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias' rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead intent on plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - trivia 
 trivia : Due to what was observed from Artorias, the phrase "falling into the Abyss" does not actually constitute entering it, but rather the near infinite and unconscious darkness of it seeking out lifeforms.
**This likely means that Wolnir was very much alive when he fell, which explains how he was able to teach grave wardens his pyromancy, though what exactly it really was that actually caused his death is uncertain.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : The Abyss is a realm of Dark born from the Dark Soul or its fragments. It's an ecosystem capable of creating life, as generated by one of the core components of the First Flame, and of expanding while slowly absorbing everything in its path; it is uninhabitable to all beings aligned with Fire including the Gods, as they require special equipment or protection to prevent corruption (both in the spiritual and physical sense). In contrast, any beings aligned with or indifferent to the Abyss (such as Humans) are able to roam it with no risk of harm or corruption.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - location 
 location : In Dark Souls the Abyss is located at the end of the New Londo Ruins. To reach to the Abyss, the floodgates must be lowered and the Covenant of Artorias ring, a reward for killing Great Grey Wolf Sif, must be worn. After climbing down a spiral staircase within a tower, the path will abruptly end, making it necessary to descend into the darkness of the Abyss.

The DLC *Artorias of the Abyss* allows us to explore a more recent Abyss, despite being located in a past era, deep within the dungeons of Oolacile.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : It is possible to reach and kill the Four Kings by killing Ingward, even if the player hasn't acquired the Lordvessel yet.
The bonfire that appears *will* allow warping to escape the Abyss, even without the Lordvessel.
**This can be used as a shortcut for far away locations, such as Anor Londo, Tomb of the Giants or Ash Lake. If the player avoids resting at other bonfires, the Abyss can be used as a "home base", warping to locations in Lordran, and returning via Homeward Bone.
Although it appears to be a black void of nothingness, the "ground" of the abyss actually floats a few meters above an unseen cobblestone floor. This can be observed by using a light source, such as the Skull Lantern or Sunlight Maggot.
Items that require hitting a surface to activate, such as Prism Stones and Carvings, will not work in the Abyss as they simply fall through the "floor".
